title: 71st RQS pilot trains to become rescue-mission qualified
description: Find out how HC-130J Combat King II pilots train and work with aircrew to complete their mission of personnel recovery.
keywords: aircrew, HC-130J, 71st Rescue Squadron, personnel recovery, Flying Tigers, Combat King, Combat King II, HC-130J COMBAT KING II, 23d Wing, 347th Rescue Group, 71st RQS, 23d WG, 347th RQG, rescue mission qualification, training, rescue, pilot, flying

transcript.text: Rescue’s unique in that we're ready to go at a moment's notice.
We're prepared to recover an isolated personnel at a moment's notice.
We're prepared to support several different mission taskings at a moment's notice.
We are able to support infiltration, exfiltration.
We're able to operate in sensitive environments, day or night, land or water.
So I'm currently in the RMQT syllabus, which stands
for Rescue Mission Qualification Training, which basically is where we get our qualifications
and certifications for rescue-specific taskings and missions.
We have certain syllabus items to complete including high-speed
air-to-air refueling, we have high-altitude air drops.
We have forward area
refueling point and hot refueling.
We have ACDTQT,
which is just wearing chem gear. Just a number of different items
that we got to complete, both ground training
for academics and then also flying
and as soon as we complete that then will be Rescue Mission Qualified.
It's not a required part of the syllabus to learn other crew members’ positions,
but it's definitely encouraged. I know it's super beneficial to know
like what the CSO’s doing back there so that you can work together better and more efficiently.
It's also beneficial to know
what the loadmaster’s doing in the back. A lot of the times we'll
just ask to ride along on a sortie just to
watch an air drop from the back just to know exactly what's going on
because every crew member has something to contribute. I'm so thankful.
I'm on a crew aircraft
because it's so much fun. It's really cool working with all these people in one aircraft.
It's not just the pilots flying. We're constantly talking to each
other and each crew member has a really important part of whatever mission we might be flying.
